T8 drive with two bearing triangles

The NEMA17 drives a T8×8 screw through a rigid coupling, with a brass flange nut inside the hollow carriage. Two fixed bearing triangles are now 40 mm apart. The longer carriage preserves 40 mm extension beyond the base exit while remaining supported at both stations. The base is 129×80 mm, with a 161 mm overall retracted length including the motor.

One rigid adjustable carrier

Both lower bearings attach to one printed carrier with two side rails and cross-braces. Four M5×25 bolts engage M5 heat-set inserts to pull it upward. Both bearings snap onto integral split axles. All six bearing seats retain Ø7.4 mm inner-ring lands and 2 mm outer-ring relief. Straight bearing journals extend into longer, 30° bent snap tips. The heads are widest at their Ø6.4 mm bearing-facing shoulders, with 0.25 mm axial clearance, then taper toward the tips.

Structural lid and mounting

The lid and recessed screw heads stay within the original 68 mm height. Six fixing points join it to the motor mount and bearing stations. Four outer base mounts use plain Ø5.5 mm through-holes for M5 bolts. Blind three-ridge M5 pilots provide four lid mounts and six mounts per side. Open 12 mm wells clear the base bolts, washers and driver from above. Motor bolts are accessible with the carriage extended. The 42 mm square output flange retains the NEMA17 31×31 mm pattern.

Print files

Four printed parts: base with snap axles, hollow carriage, shared bearing carrier and lid. All parts have individual STL downloads and a source bundle. Geometry checks do not establish load capacity, backlash or print-fit tolerances.

Geometry checks

Loading check report…

Hardware meshes are fit references. Carrier adjustment shows rigid take-up to contact, not preload force. Snap deflection is a geometric illustration, not a PETG stress simulation. Test bearing fit, insertion force, retention and creep before use.
